prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Atlanta to replace my air conditioner?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” HVAC company for everyone — the right contractor depends on your exact location in the Atlanta metro, your budget, your home’s needs, and which installers are available and doing good work right now. I can, however, help you find a highly qualified company and tell you exactly what to look for.

Quick next step
- Tell me your Atlanta ZIP code and whether this is a simple replacement (same size/location) or you think you need a full system change (new outdoor unit, indoor coil/furnace/ductwork). I’ll help narrow options and give more‑targeted advice.

What to look for (checklist)
- License & insurance: Contractor carries liability insurance and any required Georgia/local licenses.
- Certifications: NATE-certified technicians; factory training for the brand they install.
- Load calculation: They perform a Manual J heat/cooling load calculation (not just “tonnage by house size”).
- Written, detailed estimate: Lists brand/model, SEER (efficiency), tonnage, AHRI match/certification, coil type, line set, thermostat, expected run times, sound levels, and equipment warranty + labor warranty.
- Permits & inspections: They pull necessary permits and follow local code.
- Ductwork inspection: They check/measure duct leakage and recommend repairs if needed.
- References & reviews: Good recent Google/Yelp/BBB/Angi reviews and local references.
- Price transparency & financing: Clear pricing, payment terms, and available financing if needed.
- Remove/dispose old equipment: Included or defined cost.
- Energy rebates: They know about local or utility rebates (Georgia Power etc.) and can help paperwork.

Questions to ask each company
- Do you perform a Manual J load calculation? May I see it?
- What is the exact model and SEER rating you recommend, and why?
- What is included in the installation (pad, line set, controls, thermostat, permitting)?
- What are the equipment and labor warranties? Are labor warranties written?
- Will my existing ductwork be adequate, or do you recommend modifications?
- Can you provide recent local references?

Brands and efficiency
- Common reliable brands: Trane, Carrier, Lennox, Goodman, Rheem, Bryant. Match the brand to installer expertise and warranty. Higher SEER = lower operating cost but higher upfront price. In Atlanta’s hot/humid climate, aim for at least mid‑efficiency (around 15 SEER or higher depending on your goals and budget).

How to find contractors near you
- Get at least 3 written, comparable quotes.
- Use local Google reviews, BBB, and Angi; ask neighbors/homeowner associations for recommendations.
- Check NATE “Find a Technician” or manufacturer dealer locators for factory-authorized installers.

Examples of companies to consider (start your shortlist)
- Large regional/national firms with Atlanta presence often include Coolray, Service Experts, and One Hour/Benjamin Franklin franchises. There are also many highly rated local independent contractors. (I can pull a short list of top-rated local contractors if you give your ZIP.)

If you want, give me your ZIP code and whether you want basic replacement or a full system upgrade and I’ll:
- Recommend 4–6 well-reviewed local contractors to contact,
- Provide an email/phone script you can use to request estimates,
- Outline a side‑by‑side comparison template for their written quotes.
